title: Nakayama's lemma for a nilpotent ideal (surjectivity modulo I)
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $I\subseteq R$ a nilpotent ideal ($I^k=0$ for some $k\ge1$), and $u:N\to M$ a homomorphism of $R$-modules (no finiteness assumed on $N$ or $M$). If the induced map $N/IN\to M/IM$ is surjective, i.e. $M=u(N)+IM$, then $u$ is surjective. (Equivalently, parts (9)-(10) of the source: if $M=IM$ then $M=0$; if $N,N'\subseteq M$ are submodules with $M=N+IN'$, then $M=N$.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00DV (label lemma-NAK, Nakayama's lemma), part (11); proof: 'Part (9) holds because if M = IM then M = I^nM for all n and I being nilpotent means I^n = 0 for some n; Parts (10), (11), and (12) follow from (9) by the arguments used above' (i.e. (11) from (10) applied to the submodules Im(N -> M) and M, (10) from (9) applied to M/N)

proof.text: Write L = range(u). By LinearMap.range_eq_top, Submodule.range_mapQ and Submodule.map_mkQ_eq_top, surjectivity of the induced quotient map gives IM + L = M.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00DV (label lemma-NAK), parts (9)-(11) and proof

proof.text: Prove I^n M + L = M by induction on n. At n = 0, I^0 M = M. For the successor, use (I^n I)M = I^n(IM), distribution over submodule sums, and I^n L contained in L to obtain I^(n+1)M + L = I^n(IM + L) + L = I^n M + L = M. These are Submodule.mul_smul, Submodule.smul_sup, and Submodule.smul_le_right. This carries out the source nilpotent-power argument directly in submodules, without introducing the quotient M/L.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma 00DV (label lemma-NAK), parts (9)-(11) and proof

proof.text: Choose k with I^k = 0 from nilpotence. The induction yields 0M + L = M, hence L = M. LinearMap.range_eq_top converts this equality into surjectivity of u.
